issues.failure_explanation: The constraints of \eqref{eq:linearminmax} are rewritten as |p(x_j)-f_jq(x_j)|^2<=eta|q(x_j)|^2 only for representations with q(x_j)\ne0; the resulting problem \eqref{eq:linearminmax2} ranges over all (alpha,beta) and is not an alternative form of \eqref{eq:linearminmax}: the zero parameter vector gives p(x_j)=q(x_j)=0 and is feasible with eta=0, so the infimum of \eqref{eq:linearminmax2} is always 0 while that of \eqref{eq:linearminmax} is (eta_infty)^2 (and |xi(x_j)-f_j|^2 is undefined at p=q=0). Nor is \eqref{eq:rat-d} the Lagrange dual function: for L = eta(1-sum_j w_j|q(x_j)|^2) + sum_j w_j|p(x_j)-f_jq(x_j)|^2 the infimum over the free variable eta is minus infinity for every (alpha,beta) with sum_j w_j|q(x_j)|^2\ne1, and such parameters always exist; \eqref{eq:rat-d} is only the infimum restricted to the normalization manifold sum_j w_j|q(x_j)|^2=1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the construction from a well-posed primal: restrict the minimization to nontrivial parameter pairs with beta_j\ne0 for j in [ell] (equivalently to xi in R(n) satisfying the interpolation conditions) and justify the normalization sum_j w_j|q(x_j)|^2=1 used in \eqref{eq:rat-d}; alternatively drop the Lagrange-duality claim and present d(w) as a parametric lower bound certified directly by Theorem thm:q-dual.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the max-min problem \eqref{eq:rat-dual} is the Lagrange dual of the primal minimax problem is unsupported: the primal has not been reformulated and the 'dual function' is not derived from it. Only the direct arguments of Theorem thm:q-dual and Theorem thm:strongdualityRuttan can relate \eqref{eq:rat-dual} to \eqref{eq:baryInterpMinmax}, so the advertised Lagrange-dual framework must be replaced or weakened.
issues.title: \eqref{eq:linearminmax2} is not an equivalent form of \eqref{eq:linearminmax} and \eqref{eq:rat-d} is not its Lagrange dual function
issues.why_classification: The equivalence and the Lagrange-dual derivation must be replaced by a homogenization/normalization argument or abandoned, withdrawing the primal-dual claim that is the paper's stated framework; but the max-min problem, its computation in \eqref{eq:dual} and the direct weak/strong duality results survive, so no new global proof architecture is required.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement bounds max_w d(w) by the squared error eta_infty of a solution of the unconstrained discrete minimax problem \eqref{eq:bestf}, while the proof (and the later use in Theorem thm:strongdualityRuttan) needs the interpolation-constrained problem \eqref{eq:baryInterpMinmax}. The proof applies Theorem lem:baryrational2 to xi*, which parameterizes only those r in R(n) with r(t_j)=y_j for all j in [ell]; in the form \eqref{eq:baryform} one has beta_j\ne0 => xi(t_j)=y_j, and beta_j=0 forces q(t_j)=0, i.e. a pole of xi at t_j. A solution of \eqref{eq:bestf} need not satisfy the interpolation conditions and then has no representation \eqref{eq:baryform}, so the comparison d(w) <= sum_j w_j|f_j q*_tau(x_j)-p*_tau(x_j)|^2 is unjustified as written (and the conclusion cited later as \eqref{eq:rat-dual} is really \eqref{eq:weakduality}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate Theorem thm:q-dual with eta_infty the error of a solution of \eqref{eq:baryInterpMinmax} (the interpolation-constrained problem) so that xi* lies in the class parameterized by \eqref{eq:baryform}; the existing proof then goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Weak duality is not established for the interpolation-constrained problem it is used for; the squeeze in the proof of Theorem thm:strongdualityRuttan (which invokes 'weak duality \eqref{eq:weakduality}' with the constrained eta_infty), its complementary slackness \eqref{eq:complement} and the extreme-point bound of Theorem thm:extremep-2 lack the bound they invoke.
issues.title: Weak duality is stated for the unconstrained problem \eqref{eq:bestf} although the proof needs the interpolation-constrained problem
issues.why_classification: A single local change of the referenced optimization problem makes both the statement and the existing proof correct and restores every downstream use of weak duality; no argument or construction has to be replaced.

issues.failure_explanation: In Lemma lem:KKT the matrices A=\sqrt{W}[C_p,-FC_q]N and B=\sqrt{W}[0,C_q]N have 2n+2-ell columns (they contain N, of size 2(n+1) x (2n+2-ell)), whereas [\what a;\what b] has 2(n+1) entries; for ell>0 the displayed quadratic form is ill-typed. Reading A,B as the N-free matrices (which is what the identity with sum_j w_j^*(|f_j q(x_j)-p(x_j)|^2-d|q(x_j)|^2) corresponds to) is no repair: Lemma lem:KKT only yields positive semidefiniteness of N^H(\what A^H\what A-d\what B^H\what B)N, i.e. on range(N), and the N-free matrix is indefinite in general (a pure-beta direction v gives v^H H v = sum_j w_j|q(x_j)|^2(|f_j|^2-d), negative whenever |f_j|^2<d at weighted nodes). Hence the inference 'Thus 0 <= [\what a;\what b]^H H [\what a;\what b]' is invalid as written.

failure_location.quote: By Lemma \ref{lem:KKT}, the matrix $H_{\bw^*}=A^{\HH}A-d(\bw^*)B^{\HH}B$ is positive semidefinite.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the step in the reduced coordinates: put [\what a;\what b]=N\what c and apply the positive semidefiniteness of A^HA-d(\bw^*)B^HB to \what c; since N\what c=[\what a;\what b], \what c^H H \what c equals the sum sum_j w_j^*(|f_j q(x_j)-p(x_j)|^2-d|q(x_j)|^2) and the rest of the proof is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The contradiction argument showing that \wtd xi is a global solution of \eqref{eq:baryInterpMinmax} and that strong duality holds is unsupported for ell>0, and with it the complementary slackness \eqref{eq:complement} and the extreme-point count of Theorem thm:extremep-2, which assumes the conclusions of Theorem thm:strongdualityRuttan.
issues.title: Positive-semidefinite quadratic form in the proof of Theorem thm:strongdualityRuttan is applied outside the subspace where it is known
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line change of coordinates inside a single displayed chain and preserves the theorem, the complementary slackness and everything downstream; no hypothesis, statement or construction changes and no new argument is needed.

It should be noted that {\sf b-d-Lawson} cannot be guaranteed to handle \eqref{eq:baryInterpMinmax} in all cases.

issues.failure_explanation: The Output clause states unconditionally that the returned function is the minimax approximant of \eqref{eq:baryInterpMinmax}, but the algorithm returns the current iterate as soon as k>=k_maxit with no optimality certificate, and even the gap test yields only an approximate certificate when it passes. The paper itself states that convergence of b-d-Lawson is unproved for ell>0 and that the method 'cannot be guaranteed to handle \eqref{eq:baryInterpMinmax} in all cases' (the sufficient condition \eqref{eq:strongdualityRuttan} can fail, e.g. when d(\bw^*)=0), so no output of the procedure is known to be the object the contract names.

failure_location.quote: \ENSURE  The minimax rational approximation $\xi^*$ of \eqref{eq:baryInterpMinmax} represented in the barycentric formula \eqref{eq:optimalpq}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the output to 'an iterate xi^(k) of the form \eqref{eq:baryform} together with the computable gap epsilon(\bw^{(k)}), which certifies xi^(k) as an epsilon_r-relative approximate solution of \eqref{eq:baryInterpMinmax} when the gap test passes', and return without certificate when k_maxit is reached.
issues.overall_effect: The stated input-output contract of the central method is not delivered: when the iteration limit is reached, or when strong duality fails, the returned rational function may fail to be the minimax approximant of \eqref{eq:baryInterpMinmax}; only the computable relative gap epsilon(\bw^{(k)}) gives a conditional, approximate optimality statement.
issues.title: b-d-Lawson output contract promises the minimax approximant without any guarantee
issues.why_classification: The guarantee type of the algorithm's contract must change from an unconditional 'the minimax solution' to a conditional, certificate-based approximate output; the method, the certificate and all proven dual results survive, so the loss is limited but is more than a local routine fix.

issues.failure_explanation: In the denominator the residual is evaluated at x_j instead of x_i, so the denominator sum_i w_i^{(k)}|f_i-xi^{(k)}(x_j)|^rho depends on j and the updated weights do not sum to one: sum_j w_j^{(k+1)} = sum_j w_j^{(k)}|r_j|^rho / (sum_i w_i^{(k)}|f_i-xi^{(k)}(x_j)|^rho) \ne 1 in general. The update therefore does not map the simplex S of \eqref{eq:S} into itself, contradicting the initialization requirement \bw^{(0)} in S and the definition of the dual feasible set, and the quantities d(\bw^{(k)}) computed in Step 3 are no longer values of the dual function \eqref{eq:rat-d} at points of S.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the Lawson reweighting normalized by sum_i w_i^{(k)}|f_i-xi^{(k)}(x_i)|^rho, i.e. evaluate the residual at x_i in the denominator; this keeps \bw^{(k+1)} in S and leaves the iteration, its invariant and all guarantees unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: After one iteration the method leaves the dual feasible set, so the dual-ascent interpretation, the stopping test epsilon(\bw^{(k)}), the computed dual bounds and the reported errors no longer refer to the dual problem \eqref{eq:rat-dual}.
issues.title: Lawson weight update is not normalized (wrong index in the denominator)
issues.why_classification: A single index inside one formula is corrected; the iteration, the invariant \bw^{(k)} in S and every guarantee of the method are preserved with no new argument or construction.
